content.text: {"what_it_is": {"claims": [{"text": "Future Long Range Assault Aircraft Development (program element 0605241A) is a U.S. Army development program funded in the Research, Development, Test and Evaluation, Army account.", "citation": {"fact_id": "6cc7bb8ce82d5230"}}, {"text": "The program directly aligns to the Future Vertical Lift (FVL) Army modernization priority, an initiative to develop a family of vertical-lift aircraft for the U.S. Armed Forces and to retain long-term industrial-base capabilities.", "citation": {"fact_id": "9b6a09c6fa1383ee"}}, {"text": "The Future Long Range Assault Aircraft (FLRAA) is the next-generation vertical-lift aircraft designed to conduct air assault, urban assault and security, maritime interdiction, medical evacuation, humanitarian assistance and disaster relief, tactical resupply, direct action, noncombatant evacuation, and combat search and rescue in a contested, near-peer threat environment.", "citation": {"fact_id": "103df00708fe940d"}}, {"text": "FLRAA is intended to give Combatant Commanders deterrence, power projection, and tactical capabilities at operational and strategic distances, with significantly increased range, speed, mobility, and payload over current Army and Special Operations Command aircraft.", "citation": {"fact_id": "103df00708fe940d"}}, {"text": "The Army competitively awarded the FLRAA weapon-system development contract in December 2022 using a hybrid acquisition approach, and the aircraft integrates advanced technologies using a modular open systems approach with design trades to ensure affordability.", "citation": {"fact_id": "9b6a09c6fa1383ee"}}, {"text": "A dedicated MEDEVAC effort designs, develops, and integrates medical-evacuation mission equipment for FLRAA, including a Mission Equipment Package with a casualty-acquisition sensor and a modular, reconfigurable Patient Handling System to provide en-route critical care on the future battlefield.", "citation": {"fact_id": "8a1fe3ecb33f0f90"}}]}, "why_it_matters": {"claims": [{"text": "The program's total funding is roughly flat year over year, moving from $1,253,637 thousand in FY2025 to $1,248,544 thousand (about $1.25 billion) requested for FY2026.", "citation": {"fact_id": "5eb7dcb53e963efe"}}, {"text": "That is a small year-over-year decrease of $5,093 thousand (about $5.1 million) from FY2025 to FY2026.", "citation": {"fact_id": "04c8c388750d4d3e"}}, {"text": "The entire FY2026 request of $1,248,544 thousand is discretionary funding; there is no reconciliation (mandatory) component in this program element.", "citation": {"fact_id": "46710522a206e90b"}}, {"text": "The FY2026 budget request funds design updates, continues manufacturing of Prototype and Limited User Test (LUT) aircraft, initiates testing, begins production planning, and continues refinement of a digital backbone architected to meet Modular Open System Approach objectives.", "citation": {"fact_id": "103df00708fe940d"}}, {"text": "In FY2024, FLRAA achieved a successful Milestone B decision, allowing the program to enter the Engineering and Manufacturing Development (EMD) phase.", "citation": {"fact_id": "103df00708fe940d"}}, {"text": "In FY2025, funding previously planned in PE 0603801A (Aviation - Advanced Development), Project B47 (Future Vertical Lift), transitioned into this program element's Project DG5 to execute Engineering and Manufacturing Development after the Milestone B decision.", "citation": {"fact_id": "9b6a09c6fa1383ee"}}]}, "players": {"claims": [{"text": "The program is run by the U.S. Army, with funding drawn from the Research, Development, Test and Evaluation, Army appropriation.", "citation": {"fact_id": "1cc64de6e85ae89a"}}, {"text": "The Army established a Future Vertical Lift Cross Functional Team (CFT) after identifying FVL as one of the Army's six modernization priorities in FY 2017, and the effort traces to the Deputy Secretary of Defense's 2012 FVL Strategic Plan outlining a joint approach for the services' next generation of vertical-lift aircraft.", "citation": {"fact_id": "9b6a09c6fa1383ee"}}, {"text": "FLRAA is intended to support the Army, U.S. Special Operations Command (USSOCOM), and the Joint Force, reflecting the program's cross-service user community.", "citation": {"fact_id": "103df00708fe940d"}}]}, "recent_developments": {"claims": []}}
